transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Ever since my wife brought up separating, I feel like I’m not coping with it well at all and it’s throwing off how I function at home and at work. I realized I needed to talk to someone because I'm just not handling this crisis the way I normally would.
Can you describe how you've been feeling emotionally since your wife mentioned separating, such as feelings of sadness, anxiety, or detachment from others?

It’s been a complete emotional roller coaster where one minute I’m panicking that I’ve ruined my family, and the next I'm just sitting paralyzed in my car in the driveway, dreading going inside. I've also been really irritable, snapping at the kids over little things, and then lying awake half the night replaying every conversation in my head.
Can you tell me how long you've been experiencing these intense emotional swings and functional difficulties since your wife first mentioned separating?

It’s been going on for about a month now, starting almost immediately after my wife first brought up the separation. All of these difficulties really ramped up within just a few days of that conversation.
Have you experienced any significant stressors or traumatic events besides the potential separation from your wife in the last few months, or has this been the primary source of distress for you?

The separation is absolutely the primary source of my distress, and everything spiraled right after that conversation. It did happen to coincide with a highly stressful time at work where I was finalizing a major contract for a marquee client, which made juggling my focus even harder. But the crisis with my wife is what really threw me off balance.

Can you describe if there are any moments or periods where you feel completely disconnected from the emotional pain of the potential separation, or if the distress has been consistently present since the conversation with your wife?

No, I haven't had any periods where I feel disconnected or numb to the pain. It has been consistently present every single day, like a non-stop roller coaster of panic and dread where I'm constantly replaying those conversations in my head.

Can you tell me if there are any specific thoughts or memories related to the potential separation that you find yourself persistently preoccupied with, or if it's more of a general feeling of anxiety and dread about the future?

It’s really a mix of both. I constantly find myself replaying our conversations in my head and second-guessing every interaction at home, panicking that I’ve blown up my family. But there's also this constant dread about the future, like when I'm sitting in my car in the driveway, dreading going inside and wondering how I'm going to keep my life and work from falling apart.

Do you find yourself persistently preoccupied with thoughts of self-blame, worthlessness, or guilt specifically related to the potential separation, or is your preoccupation more focused on the practical and emotional consequences of the separation for you and your family?

It's honestly a mix of both. I feel a deep sense of guilt and constantly blame myself, replaying past conversations and worrying that I've completely blown up my family. At the same time, I'm highly preoccupied with the practical fallout, like how this is affecting my kids and my inability to focus on closing deals at work when my structured home life is falling apart.

Can you tell me if the guilt and self-blame you're experiencing are primarily focused on perceived failures in your relationship or if they extend to other areas of your life, such as your role as a parent or your performance at work?

While it started with feeling like I blew up my marriage, the guilt has definitely extended to other areas of my life. I feel terrible about being so distracted and snapping at my kids, which has left my wife to handle all of their logistics because I've been too unreliable. It has also bled into my work, making me worry about losing my professional focus and stalling major deals because I'm missing key details.
Have you experienced any episodes where you felt as though you were outside observers of your life, or like you were in a dream, since your wife mentioned separating?
No, I haven't experienced anything like that at all. I don't feel like an outside observer or like I'm in a dream; in fact, everything feels painfully real and overwhelming.
Have you had any experiences where you felt detached from yourself or your surroundings, or like you were 'going through the motions' without being fully present, since the separation crisis began?

I haven't really experienced feeling detached from myself or my surroundings. While I get highly distracted, unfocused, and sometimes zone out in my car because I'm dreading going inside, I don't feel disconnected from reality or my own body.

You mentioned you haven't felt detached from yourself or your surroundings, but can you clarify if there have been moments where things around you seemed unreal or distant, even if you felt connected to your own body and emotions?
No, I haven't had any moments where my surroundings or the things around me seemed unreal or distant. Everything feels very real, almost painfully so, and I'm acutely aware of what is happening.

To further clarify, are you certain you haven't experienced any brief moments, even if very fleeting, where either you felt like you were observing yourself from outside your body or the world around you seemed foggy or far away, since your wife mentioned the separation?
No, I am certain I haven't experienced anything like that. I have never felt like I was observing myself from outside my body, and the world around me has never seemed foggy or far away.
Are you absolutely sure you've never had even a brief moment where you felt like you were in a dream or things seemed unreal, even if it was just for a second, since your wife brought up separating?

Yes, I am completely sure. I haven't experienced anything like feeling in a dream or having things seem unreal, even for a brief moment, since my wife brought up separating. If anything, the reality of the situation has felt far too sharp and constant.

To confirm, you have not experienced any episodes of feeling like you're observing yourself from outside your body or feeling like things around you are unreal since the separation crisis began, correct?
That is correct, I have not experienced those feelings at all. I have never felt like I was outside my body, and things have never felt unreal to me during this time.

Can you confirm again, without a doubt, that you haven't had even the slightest feeling of being disconnected from yourself or the world around you, as this is crucial in understanding your current state?

Yes, I can absolutely confirm that without a doubt. If anything, I feel all too connected to the reality of my situation—I am just constantly overwhelmed, anxious, and worrying about the separation rather than feeling detached at all.
